profile.reading:
This is Polcom's Skawina data center, located in the town of Skawina immediately southwest of Krakow, in southern Poland. Polcom is a Polish IT infrastructure, colocation, and cloud computing company headquartered in Skawina, on ulica Krakowska, and its own materials describe the company as having operated in the market for more than 30 years, with a current team of about 170 specialists serving more than 300 business customers, roughly 70 percent of whom Polcom says do business internationally across four continents. Sources checked during this research give inconsistent opening dates for this building. One section of Polcom's own site frames Skawina as the company's first data center, in a passage describing Polcom's history as starting around 2006, while a separate Polcom announcement about its newer Alwernia facility instead states the Skawina site opened in 2011. This registry records both dates as reported rather than resolving the conflict, since no independent record settling it was found during this research.

Polcom's own facility page for Skawina describes the building as covering about 6,000 square meters and states a facility power figure of 15 megawatts, without labeling that figure as IT load, utility feed, or backup generation specifically, so this registry does not assign it to any single one of those categories. The same page describes a power supply and cooling setup engineered to support up to 15 kilowatts per rack, a 2N power distribution architecture, N or N+1 backup generator architecture, and a 2(N+1) UPS configuration, along with twelve independent network operators and two telecommunications rooms. The site holds ISO 27001:2017 information security, ISO 27017:2015 cloud security, and ISO 9001:2015 quality management certifications, and Polcom separately advertises Poland's Polska Chmura, or Polish Cloud, certification and PCI DSS compliance across its wider service catalog.

Skawina forms one half of a two site data center network Polcom operates in the Krakow region, paired with a newer facility in Alwernia, about 24 kilometers away near the Krakow to Katowice highway corridor, with the two sites linked by dedicated fiber optic cable. Polcom's own announcement of the Alwernia facility's completion, published in April 2023, put its construction cost at about 63 million zloty and described a direct liquid cooling system using magnetic bearing compressor units paired with a proprietary system for recovering heat from coolant fluid piping, which Polcom says cuts water heating energy use by about 10 percent and helps the site reach a power usage effectiveness figure below 1.2. Combined, Polcom describes the Skawina and Alwernia sites as totaling more than 12,000 square meters of data center space. No source found during this research disclosed a Tier rating, either self declared or third party certified, for the Skawina building specifically, and this registry records that as an open gap rather than assuming a rating from the certifications that were disclosed.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-06. Prior version of this row set it_capacity_mw to 15 based on Polcom's site text "Power: 15 MW", but that text does not explicitly label the figure as IT capacity or critical load per house style, so it_capacity_mw was removed from the fact box and the ambiguity is instead described in prose. Sources are all operator-owned pages (polcom.com.pl); no independent Polish permitting, municipal, or trade press coverage of this specific building was found via WebFetch this session (WebSearch quota was exhausted earlier in this session, limiting additional targeted queries for e.g. Skawina/Krakow county planning records or independent trade press). Polcom's own site gives conflicting opening-year signals for Skawina (a passage implying ~2006 as the company's first data center, versus a separate Alwernia announcement stating Skawina opened in 2011); both are reported in the reading rather than picking one. No Tier rating found for this building from any source.
